text:
Seth Jones had a month nobody saw coming. Nineteen points in 16 games, 16 in his last ten, and Sports Illustrated ran the headline "After historic month, Seth Jones a serious candidate for Norris Trophy." Last season, in a year NHL.com reports was interrupted by a foot injury, he managed 32 points in 52 games.

Our form check calls this earned, mostly. Florida is creating more with him on the ice (18.8 on-ice expected goals over his last ten games against 16.0 we'd usually expect), and his own goals match his chances almost exactly. He's playing 24:49 a night, although that's down more than two minutes over the hot stretch.

The fine print is the power play. Twelve of his 19 points have come there, and 16 points in ten games is roughly double what we'd expect at his ice time. That pace won't last. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking also flagged his exits last season: only 30% left the zone with possession.

Still, our projection now has him around 68 points, more than double last season. Norris or not, this is a start worth taking seriously.
headline: Seth Jones, Norris talk, and the fine print
